chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Fadala, from Saif ibn 'Amira, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and Kulaib al-Asadi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): that he narrated to them the Adhan, so he said:

"Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah. I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. Come to prayer, come to prayer. Come to success, come to success. Come to the best of deeds, come to the best of deeds. Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest. There is no god but Allah, there is no god but Allah." And the Iqamah is likewise.
ai.seo_question: What is the exact wording and sequence of the Adhan according to Shia hadith sources?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the canonical structure of the Adhan, notably including the phrase 'Hayya 'ala Khayr al-'Amal' (Hasten to the best of deeds), which is a distinctive feature in Shia jurisprudence. It confirms the direct transmission of the Prophet's and Imams' liturgical practices, reinforcing the theological emphasis on inviting believers to both ritual prayer and righteous action. The Iqamah's identical structure underscores the continuity between the initial call and the immediate preparation for congregational worship.
